decisive_items: Angiotensin-converting enzyme level was elevated at 77 U/L
acid-fast bacilli and fungal stains were negative
response.rationale: R2 is favored because non-caseating microgranulomas in multiple GI sites plus elevated ACE and negative AFB/fungal stains are highly specific for sarcoidosis. R3 explains the abdominal pain, diarrhea, and endoscopic inflammation but lacks the granuloma/ACE raw support and would not account for the elevated ACE. R1 is excluded by negative celiac serologies; R4 is excluded by negative Tropheryma whipplei testing.

rejected.why: Negative anti-transglutaminase and anti-endomysial antibodies plus non-caseating granulomas are incompatible with celiac disease; raw support is only nonspecific GI symptoms.
Tropheryma whipplei testing was negative, and the non-caseating microgranulomas are better explained by sarcoidosis; Whipple's disease is effectively excluded.
